idea-plugin.name: XPath Injection Sink Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags an XPath.evaluate(...)/.compile(...) call whose argument is built from an HTTP endpoint parameter -- CWE-643 (XPath Injection), the mechanism documented in the OWASP Testing Guide: an attacker's raw input becomes XPath SOURCE TEXT, re-parsed and evaluated by the XPath engine.

Built on a real, hand-written XPath 1.0 parser -- the THIRD full custom grammar in this catalog, after the ReDoS Catastrophic-Backtracking Companion's regex grammar and the SpEL Injection Sink Companion's SpEL grammar. The grammar's job here is noise reduction: it reconstructs the argument's static skeleton (every tainted operand replaced by a placeholder) and confirms it parses as well-formed XPath before flagging -- it never suppresses a real injection, only skips a call whose argument clearly isn't shaped like XPath source text at all.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only Java, only same-method taint; AWS CodeGuru Detector Library has a dedicated XPath injection detector, but it's CI/batch, not an inline IDE inspection -- no dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
